sentences.text:
Heard on I.A. No.17610/2025, which is fifth application on behalf of appellant under Section 430 (1)
of BNSS, 2023/389 (1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 5.12.2022 passed by the learned Special Judge,
POCSO Act, District Raisen (M.P.) in Special Case No.86/2021, whereby the present appellant has been convicted under Sections 366 and 376 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 05 years and 10 years respectively and fine of Rs.5000/- for each offence with default stipulation.

entities.text:
Special Judge,
POCSO Act, District Raisen (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the present appellant that earlier two bail applications dated 23.2.2024 and 16.7.2024 were decided on merits.

Other two bail applications have been dismissed as withdrawn vide orders dated 5.11.2023 and 22.9.2023 but this fifth bail application has been filed in the changed circumstances as the prosecutrix has been held major by Division Bench in another case in Cr.A.7597/2022 (Sandeep Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh) vide order dated 4.9.2024.

entities.text: Cr.A.7597/2022 (Sandeep Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the Division Bench of this Court has upon considering the evidence has found that the prosecutrix was 20 years old at the time of the offence and that her grand mother has got the admission of the prosecutrix in the concerned school and she did not know about the exact date of 2 CRA-211-2023 birth of prosecutrix.
Therefore, prosecutrix in this case who is similar was major at the time of offence.
He is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
The final disposal of this appeal will take considerable time.
Therefore, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, the remaining jail sentence of present appellant be suspended and he be released on bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for State has opposed the prayer made by the counsel for appellant and prayed for rejection of application.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record at the outset it is to be established that the prosecutrix in Cr.A. No.7597/2022 is similar with the prosecutrix of this case.
Moreover, each case has to be decided on its own merits.
Here, in this case, the relevant is the evidence led by both the parties in this case alone.
The evidence in another case cannot be read in the evidence unless it is submitted and proved by the party concerned.
Therefore, there is no change circumstances.
Already two bail applications have been dismissed on merits.

There is no substance Irfan Shah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95953293/
1 in the bail application.

entities.text: Irfan Shah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence this Court is of the considered view that this is not a fit case in which suspension of sentence can be granted at this stage.
Accordingly, I.A. No.17610/2025 is hereby dismissed.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
